newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-YORKSHIRE MEMBERS BACK MOVE TO LEAVE HEADINGLEY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-YORKSHIRE MEMBERS BACK MOVE TO LEAVE HEADINGLEY.

text.p: Yorkshire county cricket club members on Saturday backed a move to end more than 100 years of tradition and leave their Headingley ground in Leeds for a new headquarters 16 kms away.
At the club's annual meeting in Leeds, 75 percent of the 14,000 membership voted for the move to a 50 million pounds ($80 million) ground in Wakefield.

Yorkshire want test cricket to switch to their new ground -- should they move -- but the new England and Wales Cricket Board would want assurances that pitches and facilities would be of test standard.
The projected move has aroused strong passions in the county but it has been strongly backed by several of Yorkshire's top former players.
"Memories are wonderful but they don't pay the bills," ex-England opener Geoff Boycott said recently.
"Yorkshire must have control of their own ground. More than 100 years of tradition and what is there to show for it? A new ground will be wonderful -- get on with it."

Former England fast bowler Fred Trueman said: "I fully support the initiative to move to Wakefield. With Yorkshire owning the ground, the finance generated by cricket will be ploughed back into the game."
Yorkshire first played at Headingley in 1891 but the club do not own the ground.

It has been the scene of some memorable international cricket, including Don Bradman's record test score of 334 in 1930 and the compelling Ashes test of 1981 when England, inspired by 149 from Ian Botham and fast bowler Bob Willis's eight for 43, beat Australia after following on.
